_comment: steer_text over T5 *encoders*: model_kind='encoder_classification' builds T5EncoderForSequenceClassification (rebase/text/encoder_classifier.py), which never constructs the decoder. The pooled feature is a masked mean over encoder token features, and the head is a single Linear -- so there is no untrained `dense` to neutralize, and the block map sees encoder blocks only (A=12, B=24) instead of the 24-vs-48 encoder+decoder mix T5ForSequenceClassification produces.
_feature_cache: This is a DIFFERENT feature space from any model_kind='sequence_classification' run over the same base ids, so _model_tag appends the kind and these features get their own cache namespace. Caches and nearest-mean head files built under the other kind are NOT valid here.
_tuned_ckpts: All six nli6 tasks from the noreg/nonlinear run, converted by scripts/convert_t5_encoder_ckpt.py. The task<->file mapping is NOT the documented seq-6text-nli2 order: it was established empirically by scripts/identify_checkpoint_tasks.py, which reads each task's column block off the head's row-norm staircase and then scores every class-count-compatible dataset through it. True order is task_0=mnli[0-2], task_1=sick[3-5], task_2=rte[6-7], task_3=scitail[8-9], task_4=qnli[10-11], task_5=snli[12-14]; the owner scores 0.95-1.00 while the runners-up sit near chance. Do not trust a single-task offset check here: snli scores 0.75 on the mnli checkpoint purely by cross-task transfer, which is how the documented order survived an earlier verification.
_target_head: B's head is nearest-class-mean centroids over 300 support examples per class, built by: python -m scripts.build_nearest_mean_head --model-name-or-path google-t5/t5-large --model-arch t5 --model-kind encoder_classification --task snli --num-labels 3 --few-shot 300 --seed 33. --model-kind MUST match model_kind below, or the centroids describe a feature space this run never visits and fail quietly at roughly chance. A-finetuned keeps the head that came with its converted directory, so source_task_heads is deliberately NOT set -- it would overwrite that head at text_rebase.py:1005. A-pretrained's head is never read at all.
_cost: feature_regime='standard' + global_ridge is the cheap path and is architecture-mismatch-agnostic. For per-block correspondence set feature_regime='linear' and stage_2_strategy='block_ridge': B's 24 encoder blocks are then grouped down to A's 12 via block_group_strategy. That runs one forward-mode jvp per source block per batch through t5-base (~220M params), so try it only after the cheap path runs clean.
_launch: scripts/slurm/submit_text_rebase.sh <exp-name> configs/text_rebase_t5enc_steer.json [key=value ...]. Overrides are resolved into <exp-dir>/config.json before sbatch, so method_params.ridge_lambda=5.0 keeps its siblings -- unlike --method-params, which shallow-merges and replaces the whole dict.
